FACT_ID: sec03-F01 | anchor: A01
Vertical rectangles instruct or state the law, while horizontal rectangles give directions or information [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec03-F02 | anchor: A01
Diamonds warn of special conditions or hazards ahead: slow down, drive cautiously, and stand ready to stop [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec03-F03 | anchor: A01
Five-sided pentagons mark school zones and school crossings, sometimes paired so the second sign shows the crosswalk itself [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec03-F04 | anchor: A01
Regulatory signs state the law and must be obeyed; a red circle with a slash means NO, with the inner symbol naming what is banned [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec03-F05 | anchor: A01
A speed limit sign states the maximum legal speed in good weather, some roads post electronic limits that change, and rain, snow, or ice can earn a ticket even at or below the posted number [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec03-F06 | anchor: A01
Do Not Enter and Wrong Way signs mean you are heading into opposing traffic: slow at once, pull over, and turn around with care [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec03-F07 | anchor: A01
A One Way sign means traffic flows only in the direction of its arrow [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec03-F08 | anchor: A01
No Left Turn bans left turns, and because Virginia counts a U-turn as two left turns, it bans U-turns wherever posted [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec03-F09 | anchor: A01
No Right Turn, No U-Turn, and No Turn on Red each ban the named move; under No Turn on Red, wait for the green signal [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec03-F10 | anchor: A01
A Do Not Pass sign opens a no-passing zone: hold your lane behind the cars ahead even when the way looks clear [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec03-F11 | anchor: A01
Left Turn Yield on Green tells left-turners at a green light that they lack the right-of-way: stop, watch for oncoming traffic, and go only with caution [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec03-F12 | anchor: A01
Keep Right warns of an island, median, or barrier ahead: hold to the side its arrow shows [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec03-F13 | anchor: A01
Lane Use Control signs assign turns by lane: traffic in the lane must turn where the arrow points, including any special permitted movement [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec03-F14 | anchor: A01
High Occupancy Vehicle signs reserve lanes for buses and for vehicles carrying a driver plus at least the posted number of passengers [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec03-F15 | anchor: A01
Disabled Parking signs reserve those spaces for people holding disabled parking permits [A01].
Source: [A01 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0009]

FACT_ID: sec03-F16 | anchor: A02
Warning signs flag possible hazards ahead: slow down and watch for further markings, signs, signals, or work zones [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec03-F17 | anchor: A02
An advisory speed sign states the maximum safe speed for a highway exit, while a Reduced Speed Limit Ahead sign means the legal limit is about to drop [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec03-F18 | anchor: A02
Stop Ahead, Yield Ahead, and Signal Ahead signs each warn that the named control is coming: slow down and stand ready to stop [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec03-F19 | anchor: A02
A No Passing Zone sign opens a no-passing zone: hold your lane behind the cars ahead even when the way looks clear [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec03-F20 | anchor: A02
A Merge sign means two same-direction lanes are joining into one, with drivers in both lanes sharing the duty to merge safely [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec03-F21 | anchor: A02
A lane reduction sign means the right lane ends: right-lane drivers merge left when space opens, and left-lane drivers let them in smoothly [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec03-F22 | anchor: A02
Divided Highway Begins means the road splits into two one-way roadways, while Divided Highway Ends means two-way traffic resumes; keep right in both cases [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec03-F23 | anchor: A02
Slippery When Wet means slow down on wet pavement without hard braking or sudden moves, leaving extra space to the car ahead [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec03-F24 | anchor: A02
A low clearance sign bars any vehicle taller than its posted height from passing under the overpass [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec03-F25 | anchor: A02
A hill sign warns of a steep grade to check your brakes for, while a deer crossing sign means slow down, stay alert, and stand ready to stop [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec03-F26 | anchor: A02
Where horse-drawn buggies travel, slow down without sounding the horn and pass with at least three feet of clearance when clear; where farm equipment travels, slow down or stop and pass only when clear [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec03-F27 | anchor: FXsec03F27
For a pedestrian crossing, watch for people walking or riding into your path, reduce speed and be ready to stop. A bicycle crossing warns of bicycles crossing or traveling beside traffic and calls for careful driving. An additional arrow sign can identify either crossing location [FXsec03F27].
Source: [FXsec03F27 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0010]

FACT_ID: sec03-F28 | anchor: A02
School zone and school crossing signs mean watching for children and standing ready to slow or stop, obeying the limit and the crossing guards, with a second arrow sign sometimes marking the spot [A02].
Source: [A02 -> src:rdmv-va-s:virginia-department-of-motor-vehicles:handbook:pdf-0010]
